sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Oldenburg is a strongly cycling-oriented city, and its parking policy sits within that. In SrV 2023, the bicycle took 47% of trips within the city, against 43% in 2009, while motorised private transport fell from 43% to 28% [9]. The Greens and SPD majority adopted the Mobilitätsplan 2030 on 26 June 2023, with cycle streets, parking management, a feasibility study for a continuous Wallring bus lane, mobility stations and park & ride [6]. In May 2024 the council approved about 70 prioritised measures, though the parking-management, park-and-ride and bike-and-ride sub-concepts were not given high priority as a whole [7]. The Wallring study would reduce traffic lanes and limit car traffic to one direction on Theaterwall and Heiligengeistwall, and the city says all car parks would remain well accessible [8].

Street parking has become much dearer and then paused. On 27 February 2023 the council voted for stepped rises in the city-centre Zone I, from 50 cents per quarter-hour from June 2023 up to €1.30 by 2027, after fees had risen only once in 30 years [0]. By 2024 Zone I stood at €0.70 per quarter-hour, or €2.80 an hour [1]. On 25 November 2024 the council suspended the next step until an evaluation of the effects on the city centre, expecting about €1 million less revenue in 2025 [2]. Resident permits cost €100 from February 2024 and €200 from January 2025 [4], and a new resident zone G in the Haarenesch district began on 1 January 2026 [5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
Most of the centre's supply is private. The city says the public car parks in the centre are mostly privately owned. It runs an LED guidance system and an online list of free spaces, and manages about 2,900 paid on-street spaces and 152 meters [12]. Drivers can pay by app on the street since 1 November 2024 [11]. Contipark runs the Parkhaus Am Waffenplatz, listed with 617 spaces, at €2.20 an hour with a €15 daily maximum [13] and 20 charging points [14]. The August Carrée, beside the hospital, has 338 spaces at €3.00 for the first hour [15].

The city lists a 358-space park-and-ride facility at Hauptbahnhof Nord and free sites at Prinzessinweg, Marschweg, Westfalendamm, Landwehrstraße and Wechloy, all with bus links [17]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our Oldenburg data cover nine car parks with 2,381 spaces, five within 500 m of the Markt (1,368 spaces) and four more within 1 km (1,013). We have no price data of our own for them, and the sourced tariffs are those of Waffenplatz and August Carrée [13][15].

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 32% on weekdays and 25% at weekends. The fullest is the Alter Stadthafen / Cinemaxx garage (50% on weekdays, 55% at weekends, 220 spaces), followed by the Bahnhof/ZOB garage (39%), August Carrée (38%) and the Theaterwall lot (37%). Heiligengeist-Höfe (23%), Schlosshöfe and Galeria Kaufhof (24% each) are the emptiest. Within 500 m the average is 29%, against 37% for the four between 500 m and 1 km. Over the years the Cinemaxx garage rose from 18% in 2022 to 54% in 2025, while Waffenplatz stayed near 40%, at 40% in 2022 and 39% in 2025. Our feed lists Waffenplatz at 578 spaces against 617 on the operator's page. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ.
